ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a cylindrical can, with point A at the bottom and point B at the top. The thick line represents the ant's path: the path is composed of several vertical upward line segments and several horizontal circular arcs; the front horizontal arcs are drawn as solid lines, and the back horizontal arcs are drawn as dashed lines. There are 4 thick horizontal circular arcs in the figure, and each segment goes around half a circle of the cylinder. Reasoning: Unfold the lateral surface of the cylinder into a rectangle. The rectangle has height 15 cm and width equal to the circumference of the cylinder base, 30 cm. All vertical segments only go upward, from bottom A to top B, so the total vertical length is exactly the cylinder height 15 cm. The length of each horizontal semicircular arc is half of the base circumference, namely 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm; the total length of 4 horizontal semicircular arcs is 4 × 15 = 60 cm. Therefore the total distance walked by the ant is 15 + 60 = 75 cm.

method.method_draft: Unroll the cylindrical surface into a rectangle whose height is 15 cm and whose width is one circumference, 30 cm. From the diagram, first identify the bold ant path as a staircase-like path: all vertical pieces go upward from base level A to the top level B, so their total vertical contribution is exactly the cylinder height, 15 cm. The horizontal circular pieces, when unrolled, form four half-width horizontal runs, because each bold horizontal arc shown is a semicircle around the cylinder. Thus their total horizontal length is 4 × (30/2) = 60 cm. Add vertical and horizontal contributions: 15 + 60 = 75 cm.
